source.work: Cennino Cennini, Trattato della pittura / Libro dell'arte, continuous chapters CLXIII-CLXVI
source.owned_span: Tambroni 1821 printed pages 147-151, PDF pages 203-207; CLXIII opening through CLXVI final requirement for competent melting/casting masters.

provenance.owned_wording: Giuseppe Tambroni, Rome 1821 printed edition; all four continuous chapters are retained.
provenance.medieval_witness: Laurenziana Plut.78.23, copied 1437, as documented by the packet and its Milanesi/Ricotta dating notes.
provenance.pre1420_status: Not established. The selected witness is later than 1420; the packet supports a pre-1450 work attribution more strongly than a pre-1420 witness or every medieval spelling.
provenance.heading_status: All four chapter headings were supplied editorially after the manuscript stopped supplying headings; they are excluded from medieval source ownership and are not used as exact-form evidence.
provenance.witness_limit: Two locator images of BML Plut.78.23 ff.80r/81r were viewed but did not locate the selected passage; no direct diplomatic collation of the 1437 folios is claimed.

explicit_source: The text instructs, asks, conditions, references, preserves, breaks, names results, and lists possible metals.
The source explicitly says warm rose water is for a high-status model and warm fountain, well, or river water suffices for other people.
The source explicitly calls the outer shell the first form and says the nose and other parts of the new representation must not break.
The source gives practical reasons or purposes for speed, consistency, avoiding bubbles, avoiding failure, and preserving the result.
analytical_inference: FORM1 as a hardened negative mold, CAST2 as the later solid likeness, and SHELL versus EFFIGY polarity are typed identities inferred from order and survival, not native technical labels.
Material reuse of the earlier method does not prove physical reuse of GYPSUM1; the second preparation is kept as GYPSUM2.
The model's face and the later effigy are linked as representation, but they are not the same physical object.
The chapter heading's breathing interpretation is not imported as a main-text causal claim; the main text only owns the tubes, their construction, placement, and handling.
unresolved: The difficult clause about the model rising and holding the confection has both transmitted and editorially conjectured readings; neither is silently selected.
The phrase after breaking the first form that says 'after you have the first' does not uniquely identify a physical antecedent for every later metal casting.
Exact dimensions and consistency instructions are retained as source constraints, not converted into target quantities or modern engineering equations.
The source says an optional brick-powder addition is better, but supplies no measured causal comparison.

complete_clause_ownership.content: The earlier coloring discussion is declared sufficient and a useful natural-likeness practice called imprinting is introduced.
complete_clause_ownership.actuality: instructional discourse, not a report of an executed event

complete_clause_ownership.content: Choose a man's or woman's face and a young, woman, or old model; beard/hair is difficult and the beard is to be shaved.
Oil the face with scented rose oil using the coarse brush and place a cap/beretta/cappuccio.
Prepare a shoulder-length, one-span cloth and sew it around the cap from ear to ear.
Put cotton in both ear openings, route and sew the cloth at collar, shoulders and front buttons, and return to the cloth head.
Turn the model onto a carpet/table/board and prepare a toothed iron ring with the stated relative dimensions.
The companion holds the ring clear; the free cloth edge is fixed to its teeth, leaving the stated face clearance for the expected paste imprint.
complete_clause_ownership.condition: clearance chosen according to desired imprint

complete_clause_ownership.content: The prepared enclosure is where the paste is to be poured.
complete_clause_ownership.actuality: prospective instruction; no material quantity is specified

complete_clause_ownership.content: Have a goldsmith make two light brass or silver tubes, trumpet-shaped, with stated approximate length and thickness.
Shape lower ends to fit the nostrils without opening the nose; perforate the upper halves and join the tubes below while respecting the space between nostrils.
The model lies back, places the tubes in the nostrils and holds them by hand.
Use cooked, fresh, sifted Bolognese or Volterran gypsum with warm water in a basin; mix quickly because it sets quickly and keep it neither too fluid nor too stiff.
Pour the compound evenly around the face, cover the eyes last, and have mouth and eyes closed naturally rather than by force.
Fill the space to one finger above the nose and let it rest until sufficiently set.
For a high-status person such as lord, king, pope or emperor use warm rose water; for other people warm fountain, well or river water is enough.
After drying, cut away the sewn cloth with a temperatojo, knife or scissors and gently remove the tubes.
The model is instructed to rise or stand under a difficult transmitted clause, holding the compound or being held by it, and the face is gently freed from the mask/form.
complete_clause_ownership.uncertainty: transmitted and editorially conjectured posture/hand readings both retained

complete_clause_ownership.content: Put away and carefully preserve the first mask/form.
Surround the same form with a baby band extending two fingers beyond its edge.
Oil the cavity carefully with any chosen oil so the work does not fail.
complete_clause_ownership.stated_purpose: avoid failure; no stronger physical mechanism asserted

complete_clause_ownership.content: Prepare more gypsum by the earlier method; optionally mix in crushed brick powder, which the source says is better.
Take the second gypsum with glass and bowl, put it over the form, and hold the form on a bench.
Tap the bench gently with the other hand so the gypsum enters every place like wax in a seal and makes no bubbles or blisters.
complete_clause_ownership.stated_purpose: uniform entry and absence of bubbles/blisters

complete_clause_ownership.content: After filling, let the form rest half a day, or at most a day.
Tap and break the outer crust, explicitly the first form, while ensuring that neither the nose nor anything else is broken.
If the form proves weak or difficult to break, before filling saw the outside in several places but never through it; then a small hammer blow can break it.
The result is the model's effigy, likeness, or imprint; the source then refers to a great lord as the example of the result.
complete_clause_ownership.reference: the model represented by the effigy

complete_clause_ownership.content: After the first form, the said imprint may be cast in copper, metal, bronze, gold, silver, lead, or any desired metal.
complete_clause_ownership.uncertainty: the exact physical antecedent of 'this form/first form' in the metal-casting possibility is unresolved

complete_clause_ownership.content: Competent masters who understand melting and casting are required; the text does not give a full foundry procedure.

shared_form_relations: A repeated source-form family equivalent to IMPRINT must be typed by grammatical context: operation on FACE, prospective product, final EFFIGY, or representation used for later CAST.
A repeated FORM reference must preserve FORM1 through preservation, banding, cavity oiling and refill; it cannot silently become GYPSUM2 or EFFIGY.
The source's earlier-method recurrence predicts reuse of an operation schema, while distinct material identity predicts that GYPSUM2 is a new preparation.
A status context must select the WATER2 branch without changing MODEL, FORM1, or EFFIGY identity.
The residual/context pair must distinguish the optional pre-fill SAW condition from the later HAMMER break; strict surface order alone cannot move C26 before C22 without the written condition.
context_sensitive_writer_contract.no_arbitrary_terminal_rule: No new terminal per full word is permitted. The writer would assign only a finite typed role to a reusable component/frame and use whole residual plus entry context to select the already declared operator. Any group that cannot supply an actor, object, condition or result remains an unknown, not a new terminal alias.
context_sensitive_writer_contract.observable_consequence: A complete repeated process frame must preserve the relation FORM1 -> GYPSUM2 refill -> SHELL1 break -> EFFIGY, while a status-conditioned medium changes only WATER2. A universal-medium or form-fusion rival predicts a different identity/branch trace.
symmetries: global transposition of any hypothetical target code
unresolved modern duration/quantity or exact metal process
context_sensitive_writer_contract.target_binding_debt: No target passage, word, component, paragraph boundary, or language is bound. Formal GDT608 composition evidence motivates this contract but does not establish any Cennini role in the manuscript.

rivals.difference: Uses rose water for all models, erasing the source's explicit status condition.
Treats first form, second fill, shell and effigy as one physical identity, contradicting preservation and destructive release.
Does not allow the explicit before-filling saw condition to scope over later filling; it loses C26's conditional timing.

limitations: The 1821 edition is later than the desired pre-1420 threshold; no pre-1420 witness is supplied.
The headings are editorial and cannot be used as medieval exact-form evidence.
The body text is practical instruction, but the constructor's negative/positive polarity and causal mechanics are analytical abstractions.
No source equivalence to a Voynich target or writing system is asserted, and no target data were opened.
